newsitem.title: USA: NYPA restarts 965 MW Indian Point nuclear unit 3.
newsitem.headline: NYPA restarts 965 MW Indian Point nuclear unit 3.

text.p: New York Power Authority's (NYPA) 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point nuclear unit 3 was restarted after a month-long outage for various repairs, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Wednesday.
NRC, in its daily plant status report, said the unit's reactor has reached the "critical" phase and is now ready to begin generating electricity.
Tuesday, NYPA said Indian Point 3 would likely begin delivering electricity to the grid later this week.
Typically, it takes 24 to 72 hours for a nuclear unit to achieve full power after startup.

The adjacent 975 MW Indian Point 2, operated by Consolidated Edison Co of New York, is expected to resume operation by early next week after being shut January 27 to correct problems that made the feedwater valve inoperable.
